questions.question: Anil Kumar sold an article to Rajat for Rs 15,000 by losing 25%. Rajat sells it to David at a price that would have given Anil Kumar a profit of 5%. The profit percentage earned by Rajat is:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 2 i.e. 40%.

Cost price for Rajat = 15000

Cost price for Anil = \(\frac{15000}{100-25}\times100\) = 20000

Cost price for David = 20000 × 105/100 = 21000

Now, the profit percentage earned by Rajat = \(\frac{21000-15000}{15000}\times100\) = 40%

questions.question: A shopkeeper allows a discount of 30% on marked price of an article and customer also managed to get additional 10% discount on the discounted price and in this way, he get a total discount of Rs 925. questions.question: In ‘t’ years, the simple interest earned on a certain amount at the rate of 10% per annum is 5/8th of the principal amount. If the rate of interest is made three-fourths of 10% and the simple interest remains the same, which of the following statement is true about the changed value?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 2 i.e. It increases to 8\(\frac 1 3\) years.

Given:

SI = P × R × T / 100

According to question:

SI = (5/8)P

So,

P × 10 × t / 100 = (5/8)P

t = (5/8) × 10

t = 50/8 = 6.25 years

Now new rate = (3/4) of 10% = 7.5%

SI remains same ⇒ time will change

SI = P × R × T / 100

(5/8)P = P × 7.5 × T / 100

5/8 = 7.5T / 100

5/8 = (15/2 × T) / 100

5/8 = (15T) / 200

5 × 200 = 8 × 15T

T = 1000 / 120

T = 8\(\frac 1 3\) years

questions.question: If a man completes \(\frac{\mathbf{3}}{\mathbf{8}}\) work in 12 days, then how many more days will he require for completing the remaining work?

questions.question: A lady walks to her office every day from home and maintains a fixed time for the same. On one day she decreases her speed by 25%. By what fraction of her usual time will she be late on that day?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 3 i.e. 1/3.

Speed is inversely proportional to time.

Initial : New
Speed 4 : 3
Time 3 : 4

Required time = (4 - 3 )/3 = 1/3 late

questions.question: What three-part economic strategy defined India’s policy changes in the 1990s?

questions.question: Which of the following is parasitic food chain?
options: Trees → Fruits eating birds → Lice and bugs
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 1 i.e. Trees → Fruits eating birds → Lice and bugs.

In a parasitic food chain, the energy flows from larger organisms (hosts) to smaller organisms (parasites). Unlike predatory chains, it usually starts with a single large producer (like a tree) supporting many consumers, and those consumers supporting even more numerous parasites.

Explanation of Other Options:

  • Option 2 (Grass → Rabbit → Fox → Tiger): This is a terrestrial grazing food chain where energy moves from smaller to larger predators.

  • Option 3 (Grass → Grasshopper → Frog → Snake → Hawk): This is also a grazing food chain typical of a grassland ecosystem.

  • Option 4 (Phytoplankton → Zooplankton → Fish → Hawk): This represents an aquatic grazing food chain, starting with microscopic producers.

text.en: Which of the following is parasitic food chain?
text.hn: निम्नलिखित में से कौन परोपजीवी खाद्य श्रृंखला है?

hn: पेड़ → फल खाने वाले पक्षी → जूँ और कीड़े

परजीवी खाद्य श्रृंखला (Parasitic food chain) में ऊर्जा का प्रवाह बड़े जीवों (मेजबान/होस्ट) से छोटे जीवों (परजीवियों) की ओर होता है। शिकारी (Predatory) श्रृंखलाओं के विपरीत, यह आमतौर पर एक बड़े उत्पादक (जैसे एक पेड़) से शुरू होती है, जो कई उपभोक्ताओं का भरण-पोषण करता है, और वे उपभोक्ता आगे और भी बड़ी संख्या में परजीवियों का आधार बनते हैं।

  • विकल्प 3 (घास → टिड्डा → मेंढक → सांप → बाज): यह भी एक चराई खाद्य श्रृंखला है जो आमतौर पर घास के मैदान के पारिस्थितिकी तंत्र (Grassland ecosystem) में देखी जाती है।

  • विकल्प 4 (पादप प्लवक → प्राणि प्लवक → मछली → बाज): यह एक जलीय चराई खाद्य श्रृंखला (Aquatic grazing food chain) को दर्शाता है, जो सूक्ष्म उत्पादकों से शुरू होती है।

questions.question: Which of the following statements regarding ionic compounds is INCORRECT?
options: Ionic compounds have a high melting point.
Ionic compounds in solid state conduct electricity.
Ionic compounds are generally soluble in water.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 3 i.e. Ionic compounds in solid state conduct electricity.

In the solid state, the ions in an ionic compound are held together by strong electrostatic forces in a rigid crystal lattice. Since the ions are not free to move, they cannot conduct electricity.

However, when dissolved in water or melted (molten state), the lattice breaks down, allowing the ions to move freely and carry an electric charge.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements are correct?

  1. The SHANTI Bill, 2025, received final approval after the Rajya Sabha cleared it on 18 December.
  2. The Bill grants statutory status to the Atomic Energy Regulatory Board (AERB).
  3. The law removes regulatory oversight over nuclear safety.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 3 i.e. 1 and 2 only.

Parliament has passed the SHANTI Bill, 2025, completing its approval with the Rajya Sabha’s clearance on 18 December. The law modernises India’s nuclear governance by granting statutory status to the Atomic Energy Regulatory Board, strengthening regulatory independence and safety oversight. It aligns nuclear operations with IAEA norms, expands liability to include environmental damage, and recognises Small Modular Reactors as future-ready clean energy options. While safeguarding sovereignty and government control over critical materials, the Bill enables limited private participation. The reform supports India’s clean energy goals, targeting 100 GW nuclear capacity by 2047.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a mineral?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 4 i.e. None of the above.

All three — Mica, Feldspar, and Quartz — are naturally occurring inorganic substances with a definite chemical composition and crystalline structure, which are the key characteristics of minerals.

Mica is known for its shiny, sheet-like layers that easily peel apart, often used in electrical insulators.

Feldspar is the most abundant mineral group in Earth's crust, essential in rock formation and used in ceramics and glass.

Quartz is made of silicon dioxide (SiO₂) and is valued for its hardness and resistance to weathering, commonly found in sand and used in glassmaking and electronics.

text.en: Which of the following is not a mineral?

अभ्रक अपनी चमकदार, चादर जैसी परतों के लिए जाना जाता है, जो आसानी से अलग हो जाती हैं, इनका उपयोग अक्सर विद्युत इन्सुलेटर में किया जाता है।

फेल्डस्पार भू-पर्पटी में सबसे प्रचुर मात्रा में पाया जाने वाला खनिज समूह है, जो चट्टानों के निर्माण में आवश्यक है और सिरेमिक तथा कांच उद्योगों में इसका उपयोग होता है।

questions.question: Unemployment that occurs during recessions and depressions are called as _______________ .
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 4 i.e. Cyclical unemployment.

Cyclical unemployment occurs due to fluctuations in the business cycle. During recessions or depressions, consumer demand falls, leading to reduced production and layoffs.

Explanation of Other Options:

  • Disguised Unemployment: This occurs when more people are working than necessary (common in agriculture). Even if some workers are removed, total output remains unchanged.

  • Frictional Unemployment: This is temporary unemployment that happens when people are 'between jobs' or searching for their first job.

  • Seasonal Unemployment: This occurs when people are unemployed at certain times of the year because the demand for their specific labor is seasonal (e.g., harvesting or tourism).

text.en: Unemployment that occurs during recessions and depressions are called as _______________ .

चक्रीय बेरोज़गारी (Cyclical Unemployment) व्यावसायिक चक्र में आने वाले उतार-चढ़ाव के कारण होती है। मंदी या आर्थिक सुस्ती के दौरान, उपभोक्ता मांग में कमी आती है, जिसके परिणामस्वरूप उत्पादन घट जाता है और बड़े पैमाने पर छंटनी होती है।

अन्य विकल्पों की व्याख्या:

  • प्रच्छन्न बेरोज़गारी (Disguised Unemployment): यह तब होती है जब किसी कार्य में आवश्यकता से अधिक लोग लगे होते हैं (आमतौर पर कृषि क्षेत्र में)। यदि कुछ श्रमिकों को हटा भी दिया जाए, तो भी कुल उत्पादन अपरिवर्तित रहता है।

  • प्रतिरोधात्मक/घर्षण बेरोज़गारी (Frictional Unemployment): यह एक अस्थायी बेरोजगारी है जो तब होती है जब लोग 'नौकरियों के बीच' होते हैं या अपनी पहली नौकरी की तलाश कर रहे होते हैं।

  • मौसमी बेरोज़गारी (Seasonal Unemployment): यह तब होती है जब लोग वर्ष के कुछ निश्चित समय में बेरोजगार हो जाते हैं क्योंकि उनके विशिष्ट श्रम की मांग मौसमी होती है (जैसे कि फसल कटाई या पर्यटन)।

questions.question: Balakrishnabuwa Ichalkaranjikar was associated with which of the following musical gharanas?

questions.question: The first meeting of the Constituent Assembly took place on December 9, 1946, in the Constitution Hall in New Delhi, which is now known as _____________________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 1 i.e. Central Hall of Parliament Building.

The first meeting of the Constituent Assembly of India took place on December 9, 1946, in the Constitution Hall in New Delhi. This hall is now known as the Central Hall of Parliament Building. It holds great historical significance as the place where the drafting of the Indian Constitution began.

The Central Hall continues to be an important venue for joint sessions of both houses of the Indian Parliament—the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha. It symbolizes India's democratic foundation and constitutional history, marking the start of the country's journey towards becoming a sovereign republic.

questions.question: Which Constitutional Amendment Act is known as the 'Right to Education' Amendment?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 2 i.e. 86th Amendment.

The 86th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2002 is known as the ‘Right to Education’ Amendment, as it made education a Fundamental Right under Article 21A of the Indian Constitution.

This amendment ensures that the State shall provide free and compulsory education to all children between the ages of 6 and 14 years. It came into effect on 1st April 2010 with the implementation of the Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education (RTE) Act, 2009.

Additionally, the amendment modified Article 45, which earlier directed the State to provide free education to children up to the age of 14, and added a new Fundamental Duty under Article 51A(k), making it a duty of parents or guardians to provide education to their children. This amendment was a landmark step toward universal elementary education and reflected India’s commitment to inclusive and equitable growth.

  • The 61st Amendment (1989) reduced the voting age from 21 to 18 years.

  • The 44th Amendment (1978) removed the Right to Property as a Fundamental Right to prevent misuse of emergency powers.

  • The 101st Amendment (2016) paved the way for the Goods and Services Tax (GST) regime.

This amendment was a landmark step toward universal elementary education and reflected India’s commitment to inclusive and equitable growth.
